patients.summary: Jill is an administrative assistant in Holyoke with episodic migraine and opioid use disorder in long remission on methadone, who joins in 2016. Her chart runs through appendicitis, postpartum psychosis and postpartum thyroiditis after her first child, a ruptured ectopic, and a second delivery followed by stump appendicitis with abscess.

Mentions she gets her methadone through a treatment program and wants her new PCP to be able to talk with them. Explained she'd sign a separate consent for that at her visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

29 y/o woman here to establish care. Coming from another primary care office in the area; records release signed today.

HPI
1. Migraine. Has had migraines for years, no aura. Unilateral throbbing headache with nausea and light sensitivity, typically 2-3 a month, worse when she is short on sleep. Sumatriptan 50 mg works within an hour most times; rarely needs the second dose. No headaches on more than a few days a month. No new pattern, no neuro symptoms.
2. Opioid use disorder. Past IV heroin use. Entered an opioid treatment program in 2014 and has been on methadone since; current dose 60 mg daily, stable, observed dosing with take-homes. No illicit use since starting the program. No alcohol since entering treatment either. She is proud of this and wants it in her record accurately. Signed 42 CFR Part 2 consent so I can speak with the program's prescriber.

PMH: as above. No surgeries. No pregnancies.
Meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP); sumatriptan 50 mg prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: Mother - hypothyroidism, postpartum depression. Father - migraines. Maternal aunt - bipolar I. Sister - Hashimoto's.
SH: Married. Admin assistant at the community college. Former smoker, quit early 2015. No alcohol. No current drug use.

ROS: negative except as above.

EXAM
Vitals reviewed. Well-appearing, pleasant.
HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodules.
Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abdomen soft, nontender.
Skin: old track-mark scarring both antecubital fossae, no active lesions.
Neuro: CN II-XII intact, normal gait, fundi sharp.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Migraine without aura - well controlled. Continue sumatriptan 50 mg prn, max 200 mg/day; keep use under 10 days/month. Headache diary if frequency climbs.
2. OUD in sustained remission on methadone - continue with OTP. Naloxone nasal spray prescribed for home, husband shown how to use it (he is in the waiting room). Will coordinate with the program; requesting dose letter.
3. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hep C screening and hep B serologies given IV drug use history. She thinks her last Pap was last year and normal, will confirm with records. Flu shot when stock arrives in October.

RTC for physical in about a year, sooner prn.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jill - your labs from Wednesday all look good. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol and thyroid are normal. Your HIV and hepatitis C tests are negative, and your hepatitis B test shows you're already immune, so you don't need that vaccine series. Nice to meet you this week.

documents.title: Opioid Treatment Program Dose Verification
documents.author: addiction medicine
documents.body:
RE: Jill Woodward, DOB 10/16/1986

This letter is released with the patient's written consent under 42 CFR Part 2. Re-disclosure is prohibited without further consent.

Ms. Woodward has been enrolled in our opioid treatment program since June 2014. She receives methadone 60 mg orally once daily. Her dose has been unchanged for over a year. She attends counseling as scheduled and her toxicology results have been consistent with treatment. She currently has weekend take-home doses.

Please contact the program prescriber before starting any medication that may interact with methadone or affect the QT interval, and notify us of any hospitalization so dosing can be confirmed.

Medical Director, Opioid Treatment Program

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u migraine.

Had a rough stretch in Jan-Feb with 4-5 headaches a month around end-of-semester deadlines, now back to 2 or so. Sumatriptan still works. No aura, no change in character. Not interested in a daily preventive. Sleep better now that the semester is over.

Still at the methadone program, 60 mg, doing well. Naloxone at home, unused; the nasal spray is past its date so wants a new one.

Exam: BP fine. Alert, well. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
Migraine without aura - episodic, at baseline. Reviewed sleep and caffeine. If she is using sumatriptan more than 8-9 days/month we'll talk prevention.
OUD in remission - naloxone renewed.
Physical due in the fall.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT - 30 y/o F

Feels well. Migraines about twice a month, sumatriptan effective. Methadone 60 mg via OTP, no use. Not smoking since 2015. No alcohol. Walks at lunch most days.
Periods regular. Not using contraception; she and her husband aren't trying but "wouldn't mind" a pregnancy in the next year or two. Discussed folate and a preconception visit before they start trying.

Meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP), sumatriptan 50 mg prn, naloxone nasal prn.
NKDA.

Exam
Gen: well. HEENT: normal. Neck: no thyroid enlargement, no nodes. CV: RRR, no murmur. Lungs: clear. Breasts: deferred, pt preference, no concerns. Abd: soft, NT. Ext: no edema. Skin: old antecubital scarring. Neuro: normal.

A/P
Health maintenance: Pap last 6/2015 normal, next due 2018. Flu shot next month at nurse visit. CBC, CMP today.
Migraine - stable.
OUD in remission - stable, continues with OTP.
Preconception - folate when they start trying; come in first.

documents.title: Preconception Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to plan for pregnancy - she and her husband would like to start trying this summer.

Discussed:
- Methadone: continue through pregnancy; stopping or tapering is riskier than staying on it. The OTP will follow her dose through the pregnancy. Baby may need monitoring for neonatal withdrawal after birth; breastfeeding on methadone is encouraged. She had already talked with her counselor and is reassured.
- Sumatriptan: use sparingly once pregnant; acetaminophen first line. Data for sumatriptan in pregnancy are reasonably reassuring if she needs it occasionally.
- Folate: start prenatal vitamin with folic acid now.
- Former smoker since 2015, no alcohol - good.
- Family hx: mother had postpartum depression. We talked about watching mood after delivery and that she can call me any time.
- Pap due this fall; will do at physical.

Exam: vitals ok. Unremarkable.

Plan: prenatal vitamin daily. Call when she has a positive test and I'll see her and refer to OB. Physical in Sept.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 31F.

Trying to conceive since June, not pregnant yet; cycles regular every 28 days. Taking prenatal vitamin daily. Reassured - it can take up to a year. Migraines 1-3/month. Methadone 60 mg, stable, OTP. No tobacco, no etoh.

Meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP), prenatal vitamin daily, sumatriptan prn, naloxone prn. NKDA.

Exam: well-appearing. Thyroid normal size. Heart and lungs normal. Breasts symmetric, no masses, no nipple discharge, no axillary nodes. Abdomen benign. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV collected; bimanual normal, no adnexal masses or tenderness. Skin normal.

Plan: Pap/HPV, CBC, CMP, TSH (preconception). Flu shot at nurse visit in Oct. Call with positive pregnancy test.

reports.text: Indication: right lower quadrant pain, fever. Technique: grayscale and color Doppler transabdominal sonography. Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder normal without stones, wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid; no sonographic Murphy sign. Common bile duct not dilated. Both kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis or stones. In the right adnexal region there is a 3 cm fluid-filled structure with surrounding free fluid. Uterus not well evaluated transabdominally.
reports.conclusion: Normal liver, gallbladder and kidneys. 3 cm fluid-filled structure in the right adnexal region with surrounding free fluid; correlate clinically and with surgical evaluation.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE (received from regional hospital)
Date of service: 12/20/2018

CC: right lower quadrant pain x 8 hours

HPI: 32 y/o F on methadone maintenance for opioid use disorder in remission, history of migraine. Woke this morning with RLQ pain, sharp and constant, now 8 hours, worse with any movement and with the car ride in. No nausea or vomiting. Bowel habits unchanged. LMP about 3 weeks ago, normal. Actively trying to conceive.

Meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP - confirmed dose with program), prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, no alcohol, no current drug use.

Exam: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), BP 130/85, HR 95, RR 18.
Uncomfortable, lying still. Abdomen: RLQ tenderness with rebound. No guarding, no rigidity. Pelvic exam: no cervical motion tenderness, no adnexal fullness, no discharge.

Data: UA unremarkable. Urine hCG negative. WBC 12.0 K/uL, 80% neutrophils.
US: gallbladder, liver, kidneys normal. 3 cm fluid-filled structure in right adnexa with surrounding free fluid.

MDM: Fever, leukocytosis with left shift, RLQ peritoneal signs. Negative hCG makes ectopic unlikely. Differential appendicitis vs. adnexal process (ovarian cyst rupture, torsion). Exam favors appendicitis. Discussed with general surgery, who will take her for diagnostic laparoscopy.

Pain: IV acetaminophen; methadone continued, today's dose already taken at the program.
Disposition: admitted to general surgery.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain; max 6 tablets per day
Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours with food as needed for pain, for up to 5 days

reports.text: Specimen: appendix. Gross: vermiform appendix with a congested, fibrin-coated serosa. Microscopic: transmural neutrophilic infiltrate with mucosal ulceration and serositis. No perforation identified. No dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Acute appendicitis with periappendicitis. Negative for malignancy.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received by fax)
Admitted 12/20/2018 - Discharged 12/22/2018
Service: General Surgery

Diagnosis: acute appendicitis
Procedure: laparoscopic appendectomy 12/20/2018

Course: Taken to the OR the evening of admission. At laparoscopy the appendix was inflamed and distended and lay low in the pelvis against the right adnexa, with a small amount of cloudy free fluid around it, which accounts for the fluid-filled structure on ultrasound. Right ovary and tube looked normal; left adnexa normal. Appendix removed without difficulty, base healthy. Fluid suctioned and pelvis irrigated. No complications.

Post-op she had mild pain controlled with scheduled acetaminophen and ibuprofen; she preferred to avoid additional opioids and none were needed. Methadone 60 mg continued daily with confirmation from her program. Tolerating diet, ambulating, afebrile on discharge.

Pathology: acute appendicitis, no malignancy.

Discharge meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP, unchanged), acetaminophen 1000 mg q6h prn, ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn x 5 days, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: no lifting > 10 lb for 2 weeks; may shower. Surgical clinic in 2 weeks. See PCP within the week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after discharge 12/22 s/p lap appy. Pain 3/10, using acetaminophen mostly, ibuprofen once a day. Eating normally, BM yesterday. No fever. Incisions dry with steri-strips. Got her methadone dose at the program this morning, no problems. Visit with PCP 12/28 confirmed. Knows to call for fever, wound redness, worsening pain.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital f/u. Lap appendectomy 12/20 for acute appendicitis, home 12/22. Path benign. Discharge summary reviewed.

Feels much better. Off ibuprofen, taking acetaminophen once or twice a day. Eating, normal BMs, no fevers. Back to work Jan 2 (campus closed until then).

Exam: afebrile. Three port sites clean, dry, no erythema or drainage, steri-strips in place. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender at umbilical port only.

A/P: s/p laparoscopic appendectomy, recovering well. Surgical clinic visit early Jan. OK to keep trying to conceive once she feels recovered - no reason to wait from a surgical standpoint per her surgeon's sheet. Light-duty note through 1/3 per surgery.
